roles.heroLead: Behind a book-matched marble wall in Medina sits the same truth as behind any tile: neither tile nor grout is waterproof — the membrane under them is. So the assembly comes first, then a 24-hour flood test, then photographs of the proof, and only after all of that does the first piece of stone go up.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Medina, WA?
roles.costP1: Tile installation in Medina starts from the same arithmetic as anywhere — roughly $14–$26 per square foot installed for tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor, labor from $11/sq ft — though stone, slab-format porcelain and steam assemblies carry the top of that range and beyond. A standard tub-shower surround is $3,200–$6,800; a full bathroom with floor, shower and niche typically runs $6,500–$14,000.
roles.costP2: Format governs cost more than material grade does. Setting a slab-look porcelain panel dead flat, or keeping a marble herringbone's lines truly straight, is layout and labor — the invoice for the tile itself is the smaller half of the story.
roles.costNote: Medina ranges as of August 2026 — tile, materials and labor together. Your written quote from the free visit is the governing number.
roles.layersLead: Seven layers between subfloor and stone. Each failed shower we're asked to open is missing one — usually the membrane, usually because someone once saved a few hundred dollars on work that now costs five figures to reach.
roles.whyP1: Leaks keep their own counsel. Water passes grout, loads the substrate, and appears two years later as a stained ceiling or a soft run of floor — often in a finished space you'd rather not open. By then the scope is framing, subfloor, drywall and a full re-tile.
roles.whyP2: Waterproofing runs about 10% of a shower's cost. In a bathroom finished in stone, skipping it isn't a saving — it's a deferred demolition.
roles.scopeIntro: Starting figures — format, substrate and layout complexity move them, stone more than most. The binding number gets written on site, free.
roles.cardShower: The full waterproofed assembly — pre-slope, bonded membrane, flood test — then niche, curb or curbless entry and tile or stone. The costliest layer is the one that never shows.
roles.cardFloors: Baths, kitchens, entries, mudrooms and lower levels. Subfloors ground flat, uncoupling membrane wherever movement or radiant heat requires one, layout snapped before a single piece is set.
roles.cardBacksplash: Zellige, slab-look porcelain, marble mosaic or plain subway done perfectly. Outlet cuts hidden in grout lines where layout allows, edges trimmed, grout keyed to the counter.
roles.cardHeated: Electric radiant over an uncoupling membrane, resistance readings logged before and after setting, on its own circuit. Sensible only while the floor is already open.
roles.cardRepair: A cracked marble tile, tired grout, a corner gone loose. We'll tell you candidly whether it's a repair or the substrate behind it has already surrendered.
roles.cardDemo: Old tile and backer removed behind sheeting and negative air, floors and finishes protected on the way out, everything hauled. The house stays presentable throughout.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Medina, WA?
roles.faqA1: Medina tile installation runs about $14 to $26 per square foot installed — tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor combined, with labor alone from $11 per square foot; natural stone and slab-format porcelain occupy the top of the range. A standard tub-shower surround is $3,200 to $6,800, and a complete bathroom with floor, shower and niche generally lands between $6,500 and $14,000. Format moves cost more than material price: mosaics and large-format panels both take substantially more labor per square foot than 12×12 field tile.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Medina?
roles.faqA2: A standard alcove shower prices at $3,200 to $6,800 in Medina, covering demolition, bonded waterproofing, a pre-sloped pan, the tile work, a niche and grout. Steam showers, benches, curbless thresholds and full-height stone — common requests here — sit above that. The waterproofing is roughly a tenth of the total and rules out the single failure that costs tens of thousands.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Without exception. Every shower gets a bonded waterproofing system behind the finish — never cement board and thinset alone. That means a pre-sloped base, membrane carried up the walls, corners, seams and penetrations sealed, and a 24-hour flood test held, photographed and documented before tile or stone goes on. Tile and grout are decorative armor; the membrane is what actually keeps water off the framing.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Four to six working days is typical for a Medina bathroom: one for demolition under dust protection, one for substrate and waterproofing plus the 24-hour flood test, one to two setting tile, and one for grout, silicone and trim. Grout then cures for 24 hours before first use. Floors alone run one to two days; steam and stone assemblies take longer, and we say so up front.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Porcelain for anything wet or trafficked: it's denser than ceramic, absorbs less than 0.5% water and shrugs off chips — the right call for floors and shower floors even in a stone-heavy design. Ceramic and glass earn their keep on walls and backsplashes. Natural stone is beautiful, needs sealing, and deserves honest counsel about where it belongs; we give all three.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes — quietly essential under stone and porcelain, which are cold floors otherwise. Electric radiant mat adds about $11 to $16 per square foot installed, thermostat included, and is only worth doing while the floor is open. It's set over an uncoupling membrane, resistance-checked before and after the tile goes down, and wired to a dedicated circuit.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Usually. Removal and haul-away run about $3.50 per square foot, and demolition is the only way to verify the subfloor, catch rot or movement, and keep finished floor height correct at doorways — which matters doubly when adjacent floors are hardwood you intend to keep. Tiling over sound existing tile is occasionally defensible; it raises the floor and conceals what we'd rather find early.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Medina?
roles.faqA8: A typical 30 square foot backsplash in Medina installs for $1,100 to $2,200 with outlet cuts, edge trim and grout matched to the counters. Zellige, marble mosaic, herringbone and slab-look porcelain reach the top of the range — the cost lives in layout and cutting time, and in Medina kitchens the layout is usually the point.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Often, yes. Repair and regrout start at $8 per square foot — right for stained or failing grout, an impact-cracked tile or two, or shower corners due for silicone. When tiles sound hollow, loosen in a pattern, or a wall gives under hand pressure, the substrate has failed and repair merely defers the real work. We tell you which you have before we price anything.
roles.faqQ10: Which Medina neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: All of Medina — Evergreen Point, Medina Heights, Groat Point, Dabney Point and Fairweather Bay — together with Hunts Point, Yarrow Point and Clyde Hill, plus West Bellevue, Meydenbauer, Enatai, Beaux Arts Village and the rest of the Eastside, and Seattle across the bridge.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: A 2-year workmanship warranty from OC Flooring covers the installation — longer than our carpet coverage, because tile faults surface in year two, not week two. Full manufacturer waterproofing assemblies add the maker's own system warranty, and the photographs of your membrane and flood test stay on file — documentation worth having when a Medina house changes hands.
